medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Academic Success Team at the Whiddon College of Medicine supports medical students in achieving their academic goals through structured, student-centered support services. We partner with students to assess performance, identify areas for growth, and develop individualized learning plans tailored to their specific needs. Our work focuses on equipping students with evidence-based study strategies, effective time management skills, and strong test-taking techniques aligned with the demands of medical education. Through targeted skill development and structured preparation, we help students build confidence, improve performance, and develop sustainable habits for long-term success.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A students Leave of Absence is handled on a case by case basis and should be requested through the Office of Student Affairs.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Lifelong learning and continuous professional development are essential for becoming a competent physician. Medical students engage in various activities that promote their professional growth in areas they identify as important for developing their knowledge, skills, and behaviors. These activities include community service projects, intramural sports, fine arts groups, specialty interest groups, research, and professional meetings. 

At certain points during their education, students may be nominated and potentially selected for membership in Alpha Omega Alpha and the Gold Humanism Honor Society. Additionally, students may apply for positions in the Peer Academic Leaders and Peer Educational and Emotional Resilience programs. 

All of these activities provide valuable ways for students to become well-rounded, contributing members of their student community, the broader community, and the university as a whole.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
The Whiddon College of Medicine is situated in a suburban area that offers easy access to various restaurants, shopping, and the largest park system in the city, which features affordable golf and tennis facilities. Gulf Shores and Dauphin Island are less than an hour away, providing students with opportunities to enjoy some of the finest beaches in the US, along with camping, hiking, and kayaking.

USA hospitals and clinics are spread throughout Mobile and Baldwin Counties. Facilities include:

•	University Hospital, with the only Level I trauma center in the area, a comprehensive advanced stroke care center, and a unique burn center that treats everything from mild burns to complex cases. 
•	USA Mitchell Cancer Institute, which offers the latest in cancer treatments.
•	USA Children's & Women's Hospital includes the region's only pediatric emergency center, providing care for sick and injured children 24 hours a day.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Most medical students choose to live off campus due to the many safe and affordable housing options within a 5-mile radius of the campus. With the relative low cost of home ownership in the Mobile area, many students have found buying a house or condo more cost-effective than leasing.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The Whiddon College of Medicine offers several organizations to support our medical students. Notably, MedPride and Allies is a student organization for those who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer (LGBTQ). Its goals include increasing the visibility of LGBTQ students, fostering a supportive and welcoming community within the healthcare system, and raising awareness of the specific needs of LGBTQ patients.  Additionally, we have a chapter of the American Medical Women's Association (AMWA). AMWA is the oldest multispecialty organization dedicated to advancing women in medicine, advocating for equity, and ensuring excellence in healthcare.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The University provides support for students with physical, psychological, or learning disabilities through the Center for Educational Accessibility & Disability Resources (CEADR). The Whiddon College of Medicine is committed to training qualified students with disabilities and works in partnership with CEADR to provide reasonable accommodations. Students seeking accommodations are responsible for initiating the request and submitting the required documentation directly to CEADR. While the Office of Student Affairs can assist with connecting students to CEADR, accommodations are granted only to those who complete the designated process and are formally approved.  https://www.southalabama.edu/departments/ceadr/
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The Wellness Program at the University of South Alabama College of Medicine is a student-led initiative that is supported by the institution. Its goal is to enhance all aspects of health and well-being among our medical students while fostering a sense of community, camaraderie, and resilience. Given the critical importance of physician resilience, medical students need to develop healthy and sustainable habits during their time in medical school, which they can carry into their professional lives.

Compassionate and competent physicians prioritize patient well-being in their practices. A key factor in ensuring patient well-being is a clinician’s ability to understand and manage their own health. Our program places medical students at the forefront of our efforts, promoting self-awareness and teaching strategies to enhance well-being. This approach enables students to provide competent and compassionate care in the future. https://www.southalabama.edu/colleges/com/currentstudents/wellness/
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The Frederick P. Whiddon College of Medicine at the University of South Alabama cultivates a family-like atmosphere where students, faculty, and staff build meaningful connections and foster a strong sense of belonging. The campus culture emphasizes academic excellence, collaboration, and a shared commitment to advancing healthcare, while also prioritizing student well-being. A robust network of support services and resources ensures students have access to the guidance and tools they need to thrive personally and professionally. With an environment rooted in mentorship, teamwork, and compassion, the college not only prepares students to excel as leaders in medicine but also nurtures their holistic development, creating a tight-knit community that feels like home.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Public transportation in Mobile is limited and accessing campus or hospital facilities without a vehicle can be challenging.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: There is a dress code when students are in the clinics, simulation labs and standardized patient exercises.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Faculty office hours are announced prior to each teaching module.  A peer tutoring program is available through the Office of Student Affairs for students who are deemed to be at academic risk.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin patient interaction in October of the first year.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lecture, with significant team-based and active learning exercises as well as simulation and standardized patient experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin in the third year.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Students are strongly encouraged to attend lectures but they are not required. However, active learning and team-based exercises are mandatory.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The Curriculum is competency-based across four years. The first two years are an integrated organ systems-based curriculum with enhanced integration for the third and fourth years. This educational model utilizes core competencies of medical knowledge, patient care, practice-based learning and improvement, interpersonal and communication skills, professionalism, and systems-based practice. The basic science component covers concepts of cell and molecular biology, structure and function, pathogenesis of disease, and pharmacotherapeutics with the goal of providing a fund of knowledge applicable to the foundations of human health. The third-year has six clinical clerkships: medicine, surgery, pediatrics, psychiatry/neurology, obstetrics-gynecology, and family practice. The fourth-year is composed of nine rotations of four weeks each. Students are required to select one rotation each in clinical neuroscience, surgical subspecialties, ambulatory care, primary care, subspecialty in medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Training students to provide primary care to rural and underserved areas is a priority for the College of Medicine. A strong scholarship program for those interested in providing care to rural and underserved communities and participation by students in primary care and rural medicine interest groups helps encourage students to consider primary care specialties. The College of Medicine also supports the Primary Care Pathway (PCP) optional longitudinal educational track.  The PCP is for students interested in the primary care specialties of Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, and Pediatrics. In addition to the core medical education curriculum, the PCP provides students training in the following areas: population health, interprofessional teams, high-value care, quality improvement, patient safety, culturally-responsive medicine, behavioral health, and leadership. Participating students experience primary care in clinics located in rural and/or underserved areas.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The medical school offers a variety of summer opportunities in both basic science and clinical research. These research projects are open to both incoming first-year students and rising second-year students. The research includes a stipend and involves an oral or poster presentation at the end of the summer. A significant number of research projects result in a publication. Students, who are research-oriented, may choose to continue these projects throughout their medical school training and graduate with Research Honors.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students are involved in a variety of community service activities in the Mobile, AL region.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Students may participate in the M.D. with Research Honors program which requires the student to present and defend their research to a selected committee.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: The Frederick P. Whiddon College of Medicine owns and operates three hospitals as well as the USA Mitchell Cancer Institute. We also have an affiliation with Alta Pointe.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/Fail with a numeric system for ranking students.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The Frederick P. Whiddon College of Medicine of the University of South Alabama was approved by the Board of Trustees of the university in 1967; the Alabama state legislature passed a resolution authorizing the college on August 19, 1967. The college admitted a charter class in January 1973. The basic medical sciences are housed on the university campus. The University of South Alabama Medical Center, operating continuously since 1831, has provided clinical medical education for more than a century. It is the major physician-staffed emergency facility in South Alabama and has been named a Level I trauma center by the Alabama Committee on Trauma. Other clinical training facilities include the USA Children's and Women's Hospital, and the USA Mitchell Cancer Institute.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: “Our mission is to provide innovative research, education, and clinical care in a culture of excellence, discovery, and scholarship to the next generation of physicians, scientists, and educators to advance patient-centered and equitable healthcare.”

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Graduate students enrolled in a degree-granting program must submit a letter of evaluation written by the major advisor or department chair containing the anticipated date the degree requirements will be fulfilled.  Consideration will be given to non-traditional applicants in the makeup of their letters who have not completed academic work in 5 or more years. Interested applicants should contact our office for more information.  If you are currently employed, we strongly encourage a letter of recommendation from your employer.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Letters from Pre-Health Committees are preferred over individual letters. If a student chooses to submit individual letters, at least 2 of those letters are required to come from faculty that have taught them with at least 1 of those letters coming from science faculty. The additional letter should come from someone who has known and observed the applicant on a personal basis.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: The interview day begins at 9:00 AM with a welcome, that includes information about financial aid as well as how the admissions process works, this is followed by their interviews at 10:00 AM and 11:00 AM. After the interviews, the applicants meet virtually with medical students for an informal information session that includes time for questions, after which they go to breakout rooms to meet in small groups with current students for more insight about the Frederick P. Whiddon College of Medicine from the student perspective. They then come back to the main room for a short closing session led by the admissions team.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Early Decision interview invitations go out in the first week of September; all other invitations begin in mid-September.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Students meet one-on-one with two interviewers. Interviews last 30 to 45 minutes each and are conversational.  Interviews will be virtual for the 2026-2027 interview cycle.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Interviews will be virtual for the 2026-2027 cycle.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: US Citizens and Permanent Residents with an MCAT score of 495 or higher.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: Applications are accepted from Alabama residents as well as Escambia and Santa Rosa counties in FL and Jackson, Harrison, George, Stone, Perry and Greene counties in MS.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Only international applicants that hold permanent resident status are considered for admission.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Out of State applicants are required to have a minimum score of 508 on the MCAT and  a 3.80 overall GPA. We give preference to those applicants that have strong ties to the state of Alabama.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: Applicant must be a permanent resident.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
For the 2026-2027 admissions cycle, accepted students to the Frederick P. Whiddon College of Medicine are expected to follow the Choose Your Medical School Tools guidelines as they relate to notifying medical schools concerning where they plan to attend. 

In light of the COVID-19 pandemic, The Frederick P. Whiddon College of Medicine has carefully reviewed the requirements for admissions. We will accept Pass/Fail grading for prerequisite coursework completed in the Spring semester of 2020. We will accept online coursework for prerequisite courses completed in the Spring, Summer, and Fall semesters of 2020 and will look at online coursework completed in the Spring semester of 2021 on a case-by-case basis.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The Admissions Committee considers the most recent MCAT score.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Applicants must have an MCAT score of 495 or higher to be considered for review.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Applicants are strongly encouraged to complete all prerequisite science courses and their corresponding labs at a traditional 4-year institution.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Letters of intent and significant updates may be emailed to COMadmissions@southalabama.edu.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The Frederick P. Whiddon College of Medicine’s Technical Standards outline the minimum physical, cognitive, and behavioral abilities required to successfully complete the curriculum and graduate as a competent, professional physician. Candidates for the M.D. degree must demonstrate skills in five core areas: the ability to observe patients and clinical demonstrations; communicate effectively with patients, families, and healthcare teams; perform essential motor tasks for examination, diagnostic procedures, and basic patient care; apply intellectual and quantitative reasoning for problem-solving and clinical decision-making; and exhibit the emotional health, professionalism, adaptability, and resilience necessary to provide effective patient care.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The Office of Financial Aid coordinates the programs of assistance available to medical students demonstrating financial need. Scholarships are also available for entering freshmen and medical students who have demonstrated academic excellence and/or financial need.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: The waitlist is a ranked list and students are accepted in the order they were ranked by the Admissions Committee.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Statistics/Biostatistics and Immunology are recommended but not required.  Biochemistry may be substituted for Organic Chemistry II.    It is strongly recommended that all prerequisite science courses and their labs be completed in person rather than online.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: We do not have a time limit as to when undergraduate prerequisite course work was completed.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Committee on Admissions will consider candidates whose undergraduate grades and scores on the MCAT indicate that they can handle the rigorous curriculum of the College of Medicine. However, admission is based on more than scholastic achievement. Applicants will be considered on their potential to become conscientious and capable physicians. The University of South Alabama provides equal educational opportunities and is open to all qualified students without regard to race, creed, national origin, sex, or handicap with respect to all of its programs and activities. Because the college is state-supported, preference is given to Alabama residents. However, highly qualified out-of-state applicants are seriously considered. Disadvantaged, rural, and minority residents are strongly encouraged to apply. Fee waivers, based solely on economic need, are granted, when documented.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: It is highly recommended that students have shadowing experiences where they are able to watch and learn from the interaction between patient and physician. Primary Care physician shadowing is looked upon favorably by the Admissions Committee. Although there is no specific number of hours required students should be able to discuss in detail what they learned from their shadowing experiences.
